- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.5) and forecast is rising, reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If recent history shows strong upward momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive rising prices) and sentiment is neutral/positive, model tends to overestimate — cap forecast slope to match recent mean.  
- If forecast spikes sharply after a dip (e.g., +10%+ from prior low), reduce by 5–15% to account for lagged market reaction.  
- When sentiment is positive and forecast is below recent 7-day average, increase forecast by 2–5% to reflect sentiment-driven momentum.  
- If forecast consistently overestimates by 2–5% in early days of a 30-day window, apply a 1–2% downward bias to the first 5–7 days.  
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–0.3+), reduce forecast variance by 10–20% to avoid overfitting to short-term noise.
